title: Leicester announce new senior management structure
content:
Leicester City have announced a new senior management structure at the struggling Championship club.

Finance director Kevin Davies is stepping up to become the new chief executive officer, overseeing the business and financial side of the club, while director of football Jon Rudkin is assuming the role of chief football officer, overseeing all aspects of the football side of the club, including the women’s team.

Davies and Rudkin will report to the club’s board of directors, made up of chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha and vice-chairmen Apichet Srivaddhanaprabha and Liu Shilai.

James McCarron has joined the club in a newly created sporting director role after leaving his position as director of player development at Belgian second division club Lommel SK. McCarron will work closely with head of recruitment Martyn Glover on player identification and recruitment.

Interim managing director Kamonthip Netthanomsak will continue in her role to be a link to chairman and owner Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha, who had been acting as CEO after the departure of Susan Whelan in October.

The club has also appointed a new commercial director, Russell Jones,

Davies was born in Leicester and has been with the club since 2011. He worked as financial controller until April 2023 when he stepped up to finance director following the departure of Simon Capper to Newcastle United.

Sources at the club, who wish to remain anonymous to protect relationships, say Davies is widely regarded as a good operator and stepped in when the club were facing financial difficulties around profit and sustainability rules.

Leicester were charged with three counts of breaching profit and sustainability rules (PSR) by the Premier League for the 2023-24 season and Davies represented the club at the hearing before an independent commission, after which Leicester were given a six-point deduction. The Premier League had sought a 12-point deduction but the commission noted the club’s efforts over the last couple of years to get their finances back under the PSR threshold.

The Premier League and Leicester City have both appealed against the sanction.

Rudkin has been with the club for over 30 years, initially as an academy coach and then academy director until he stepped up to become the club’s director of football in December 2014.

Leicester won the Premier League title in 2016, reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League the following season and won the FA Cup for the first time in 2021, while also reaching the semi-finals of the Conference League. But they have been on a remarkable slide since and now face the prospect of a third relegation in four seasons and a second ever stint in League One.

Rudkin has been the focal point of much of the discontent of disgruntled fans, who have protested in recent seasons. Last Saturday a fan protest before the home defeat to Norwich City also called for the club to be sold.

Srivaddhanaprabha, known as Khun Top, said the appointments were designed to provide defined leadership in crucial areas of the club’s operation and to ultimately re-establish the club in the Premier League.

“Our commitment to this club and to our supporters remains unwavering,” chairman Khun Top said in a statement. “We want to build a leadership structure that best reflects the demands of the modern game and the specialisms necessary for us to excel in an increasingly competitive environment.

“Kevin has been a powerful, stabilising force behind the scenes during a difficult period of adjustment for the club and has demonstrated the skills to lead, develop and align our key business functions and the overall strategy that guides them.

“Jon’s knowledge of the club, its football culture and the wider football landscape is extensive and complements those skills in a way that sets us up strongly for this next phase of the club’s growth.

“We remain committed to greater transparency and levels of engagement with our supporters as part of our vision.”
